target: CRCFT modes formalization as 5-track verified foundational typed condition

theorem_statement.name: CRCFT Modes
theorem_statement.statement: For typed cascades with diagnostic-complete state and named external classical theorem dependency, the cascade's bridge defect or residual decomposition classifies into three typed modes: TE target-equivalence, CTMT carrier-typed matrix-element terminality adapted to the carrier, and BF bridge-failure. Each component classifies into one or more of these modes, and the terminal object form adapts by track while preserving the three-mode taxonomy.

modes.label: Target-Equivalence
modes.definition: Closure of the component is logically equivalent to the cascade target conjecture; no non-circular proof of the component yields the target.

modes.label: Carrier-Typed Matrix-Element Terminality
modes.definition: The component reduces to a carrier-native terminal family not decidable from inherited records, such as matrix elements, component maps, cycle columns, PDE estimates, or package atlases.

modes.label: Bridge-Failure
modes.definition: The cascade bridge, comparison, or transport between sub-objects fails; no audited bridge transports closure.

proof_outline: Each audited track reaches a diagnostic-complete or framework-frontier state with named external dependencies and decomposed residuals or gates.
For every component, closure attempts fall into target-equivalence, carrier-native terminal reduction, or bridge/comparison failure.
The five tested tracks classify all documented components into TE, CTMT, BF, or documented mixed forms such as TE with CTMT substructure.
The terminal object adapts to the domain but the typed-condition shape is preserved.
The result is a candidate framework theorem supported by multi-instance evidence, not a category-theoretic proof.

adaptation_sub_finding.name: CTMT terminal-object adaptation under CRCFT modes
adaptation_sub_finding.summary: CTMT preserves the typed terminality shape while replacing literal matrix elements by the native terminal object of the track.

retained_nogos: No claim that RH, BSD, Hodge, NS, or P-vs-NP is solved.
No claim of category-theoretic proof or universal theorem beyond the candidate verified-on-5-track status.
RH retained no-gos, including Bridge Impossibility and non-transport of non-CRE closures, remain active.
BSD retained no-gos, including noninjective public shadows such as finite scalar BSD factor and dim Sha[p], remain active.
Hodge retained no-gos, including missing column/cycle realization and public-shadow non-promotion, remain active.
NS retained no-gos, including energy/enstrophy-only, packing-only amplitude, moving-window, and raw-nonlinearity shadows, remain active.
P-vs-NP retained no-gos, including universal P-machine atlas TE, no-smuggling, fixed quotient non-descent, and local-status non-promotion, remain active.
